name: Quote-to-Order convert (price lock + order-level reprice)
what_it_tests: Order created from quote locks the final quote prices (list/discount/regional/COLA) onto OrderItems; an order-level Reprice-All re-runs the procedure on OrderItem context with the correct contributor base and term fields, producing identical results with no contextDefinition gack
proc_mechanism: Convert flow copies quote lines; Stamp Contributor Base (Pre-Discount) + Stamp Base Filter; Pricing Effective Dates; whole procedure re-evaluated on OrderItem context
expected_behavior: OrderItem.UnitPrice matches final QuoteLineItem price; order reprice identical to quote; no contextDefinition gack; term fields populated
test_setup: Convert close-won quote to order then Reprice-All, mixed lines

prior_run.actual: Order 00095649 (mixed: beSECURE UnitPrice 206/Net 206/TLA 412/PTC 1/End 2027-06-28; Cobalt Strike list 5900 locked UnitPrice 5900/Net 5900/TLA 11800/PTC 1) Force reprice isSuccess=true errorResponse=[] no gack, all values identical, TotalAmount 12212, CompletedWithPricing/Validation null. Order 00095620 (5250 Integrator perpetual 3675 PTC 0 no End + subscription 2021.25 PTC 1 End 2027-06-25) reprice isSuccess=true no gack, identical, TotalAmount 5696.25.
prior_run.notes: Order-level Force reprice via REST place action on Order+OrderItem graph (contextDef SalesTransactionContextExt_v2 / OrderEntitiesMapping). Tested on 2 distinct mixed-line converted orders; both idempotent + gack-free, validating SC-3308/SC-3371/reprice-contextDef P0 risk is closed. Note: source QuoteLineItem snapshot fields (UnitPrice/NetUnitPrice) read 0 even on a CompletedWithPricing quote after a successful Force reprice (RLM stores pricing in runtime context, not the QLI snapshot) - so the price-lock is evidenced by OrderItem prices matching the correct configured/list catalog values, not…
